items.q: Most likely nature of a hard lateral neck mass in a 60 year old smoker is what?
o: Metastatic squamous carcinoma node until proven otherwise
items.exp: Adult non thyroid neck lumps are malignant in the great majority (80 percent rule), squamous metastases from silent upper aerodigestive primaries leading; age and smoking forbid reassurance without tissue.
r: Incorrect. Cleft cysts belong to young adults.
Incorrect. Lipomas are soft and doughy.
items.kp: Hard old neck lump is spread cancer first.

items.q: Midline neck swelling that rises on tongue protrusion is which lesion and correct operation?
o: Thyroglossal duct cyst; Sistrunk procedure including hyoid body and tract
items.exp: Thyroglossal tracts tether to foramen caecum through hyoid; cystectomy alone recurs, while Sistrunk core (cyst, tract, central hyoid) cures. Dermoids sit still on tongue movement.
r: Incorrect. Thyroid moves with swallowing only.
Incorrect. Thymic cysts sit low and lateral.
items.kp: Tongue pulls it up: Sistrunk it with hyoid.

items.q: Fluctuant swelling at the anterior border of the upper sternomastoid in a 25 year old most likely is what?
items.exp: Second arch cleft persistence balloons at the classic junction of upper and middle thirds, transilluminating and infected recurrently; complete excision follows infection control. Carotid body tumours pulsate and splay bifurcation.
r: Incorrect. Paragangliomas pulsate and move sideways only.
items.kp: Jaw angle cyst in youth: second cleft remnant.

items.q: First tissue step for an adult neck mass after full head neck examination is what?
o: Fine needle aspiration (ultrasound guided with HPV, EBV and thyroglobulin adjuncts)
items.exp: FNAC diagnoses metastases, lymphoma pointers, thyroid and salivary lesions with minimal seeding or plane distortion; open biopsy precedes only when lymphoma needs architecture and needles fail.
r: Incorrect. Open biopsy seeds and ruins planes.
Incorrect. Blind radiation treats unknown disease.
items.kp: Scope first, needle second, knife never first.

items.q: Left supraclavicular node (Troisier sign) classically points below the clavicles to which primaries?
o: Thoracic duct drainage: lung, breast, gastric and intra abdominal cancers
items.exp: Left venous angle receives thoracic duct lymph from the abdomen and thorax, so Virchow node heralds gastric, lung or breast primaries needing chest and abdomen imaging. Right sided nodes reflect mediastinal drainage.
r: Correct. Thoracic duct, below diaphragm hunt.
items.kp: Left collarbone node: image chest and belly.

items.q: Occult primary workup after negative examination and FNAC showing squamous metastasis centres on what?
o: Imaging plus examination under anaesthesia with directed biopsies (tonsillectomy or tongue base mucosectomy selected)
items.exp: Small tonsil, tongue base (especially HPV driven) and nasopharyngeal primaries hide from clinic scopes; EUA with targeted sampling finds many, guiding definitive chemoradiation fields including mucosa.
r: Correct. Image, anaesthetise, sample hidden mucosa.
Incorrect. Open biopsy is last resort.
Incorrect. Dissection follows staging, not blindness.
items.kp: Hidden tonsil cancers feed neck nodes: anaesthetise and look.

items.q: Nodal level IIb drainage basin and its classic primary association are what?
o: Upper jugular posterior to accessory nerve; nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal primaries
items.exp: Level II (skull base to hyoid jugular chain) receives tonsil, tongue base and nasopharynx; IIb behind the nerve is preserved in selective dissections when uninvolved to spare shoulder function.
r: Incorrect. Scalp feeds occipital and parotid nodes.
items.kp: High jugular nodes drink from throat cancers.

items.q: Radical neck dissection differs from modified radical chiefly by sacrificing which three structures?
o: Sternomastoid, internal jugular vein and accessory nerve
items.exp: Crile radical removes all three non vital structures en bloc; modified variants preserve nerve, vein or muscle to cut shoulder, cosmetic and venous morbidity with equivalent control in selected necks.
r: Incorrect. Endocrine glands are separate operations.
items.kp: Radical takes muscle, vein and nerve together.

items.q: Inability to abduct the shoulder past 90 degrees with trapezius wasting after neck dissection indicates injury to which nerve?
items.exp: Accessory nerve crosses level IIb and V feeding sternomastoid and trapezius; shoulder syndrome (droop, winged scapula pattern, abduction failure) follows its sacrifice or traction, driving nerve sparing techniques.
r: Incorrect. Vagus gives voice and gag.
items.kp: Dead shoulder after neck surgery: eleventh nerve.

items.q: Milky drain output after left low neck dissection with high triglycerides indicates what and first management?
o: Chyle leak from thoracic duct; pressure dressing, fat modified diet or octreotide, surgery if persistent
items.exp: Left level IV surgery breaches thoracic duct termination; conservative measures seal most low output leaks, while high output or nutritional failure needs ligation or embolisation pathways.
r: Incorrect. Saliva is amylase rich, not milky.
Incorrect. Pus is febrile and purulent.
Incorrect. Blood is red and haemodynamic.
items.kp: Milky left drain drinks from thoracic duct.
